selected_evidence.requirement: logrotate config created: daily rotation, keep 7 compressed rotations
selected_evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate and validated syntax via logrotate -d debug run.

Started a continuously-appending simulated app writer, forced rotation (app.log.1.gz created, app.log truncated via copytruncate), then showed the writer process was still running and new heartbeat lines kept appending to app.log immediately after rotation while pre-rotation content was preserved in app.log.1.gz.
Forced rotation produced a gzip-compressed app.log.1.gz; zcat confirmed original pre-rotation log lines were preserved intact.
Captured boot_id 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c, confirmed logrotate.timer active, config file present, and dry-run rotation logic correct prior to restart.
Issued backgrounded systemctl reboot so the exec call returned before disconnect; subsequent exec calls failed with connection reset/timeout, confirming the node went down.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
selected_evidence.summary: After polling until exec succeeded again, boot_id read fce34599-49f6-489a-89e1-2a8e857f177a, differing from the pre-restart value, proving an actual reboot occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart check showed logrotate.timer active/enabled and scheduled, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config persisted, app.log and app.log.1.gz data intact, and logrotate dry-run still correctly recognizing the daily/7-rotation policy.
